answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks using an invite-graph debt mechanism, where every new identity incurs costs based on the number of downstream identities. When an identity is created, the inviter pays a toll that increases with each additional identity they bring in As the gale of new identities blows, costs mount—imagine an initial fee of 10 tokens rising to 100 tokens for the tenth identity invited. This structure discourages farming by making it financially unsustainable, akin to a lotus flower whose roots demand ever more nourishment from the muddy inlet as it expands.
